recipes.name: Refreshing Summer Orzo Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) bag fresh spinach leaves, chopped

steps.text: Bring chicken broth to a boil over high heat. Add orzo pasta and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain well, then pour orzo into a bowl and toss with butter to keep it from sticking; set aside.

While pasta is cooking, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in garlic and cook until garlic softens and the aroma mellows, about 2 minutes. Stir in pine nuts, basil, thyme, and red pepper flakes. Cook and stir until pine nuts have toasted to a light golden brown.
Stir pine nut mixture into orzo along with olives, capers, and feta cheese. Toss in spinach and lemon juice.
Serve either warm or cold, but it's better the next day.

raw_recipe.headline: Refreshing Summer Orzo Salad
raw_recipe.description: This summer orzo pasta salad features pasta, olives, feta, and spinach for a wonderful, light dish. It goes well with tuna or grilled chicken as well.

review.reviewBody: This salad has good flavor. I especially liked the touch of thyme. I used reduced sodium broth but with feta, capers and kalamata olives it was a bit salty. Next time I would omit the broth and cook the orzo in unsalted water. With all the other great flavors I don't think the broth would be missed. I would also omit the butter and just rinse the pasta to eliminate any sticking. I used fresh basil and thyme and added grape tomatoes to cut the salt taste, it was a nice addition. Did a dry toasting on the nuts and drizzled the oil in the salad. Diced chicken would go very well in this salad. Thank you for the post.

Instead of using butter to keep the orzo from sticking I used about 1 cup of premade pesto. That also added a really nice light green color to the salad. I would only use a 1/8 cup of olive oil to sauté the garlic basil thyme and red pepper flakes.Try sautéing these herbs on medium low as medium was a bit too high and browned the seasonings more than I like. Also, I doubled all of those seasonings since I like more spices in my dishes. I think it’s salty enough so I’m glad I didn’t add the juice from the capers. To add more color, I added one cup of quartered grape tomatoes. The taste of this salad is amazing! Serving it cold at a baby shower tomorrow, can’t wait to see what everybody thinks!

First let me say that this is a great side salad. Had it with pork loins tonight and it was well received. Now for the problems...4 cups of broth is not enough liquid for a whole box of orzo. I eyeballed it and ended up with 3/4 of a 16 oz box stirred into boiling broth. Pop the lid on and in 10 minutes or so we had no liquid left. Stirred it well several times while cooling down as well as throwing in the chopped baby spinach to let it wilt. Toasted the pine nuts dry and set them aside. Used the butter to help with sticking and added garlic flavored olive oil as well...just a drizzle. Let this cool down stirring every ten minutes or so. When cool add diced shallot, feta, olives and pine nuts. I also added some chopped grape tomatoes. This seemed dry after a few hours though not sticky. I did add a very small amount of Greek salad dressing and stirred it in. It added great flavor but kept the nongreasy texture. Makes a lot but will make good lunch. Mikomine

Made it for our garden club lunch. It was well loved by everyone, recipe requested quite a few times. I followed the recipe, but didn't cook orzo in chicken broth. I just used salted water. I did add some fresh basil and halved grape tomatoes. I toast my pine nuts by rinsing in cold water very briefly in colander, then add 1/2 tsp. salt, put in paper bag and put in microwave on high for 1 - 2 minutes. Quick and easy. I also put the spinach in bottom of colander before I poured the orzo and cooking water over- instantly wilted. I will definitely make this again. In fact I'm making it this weekend for a picnic.

I initially found this recipe in 2007; I used a mediterian flavored feta cheese and wilted the spinach. First day served as a warm salad as I failed to cool the orzo! This resulted in a slightly creamy salad; It was delicious then and just a good the next day cold!

Great salad! I added half a cup of wild rice (cooked). No butter, no capers, no extra olive oil (except for a tiny bit to sauté the garlic). Added sun dried tomatoes, A LOT of spinach, roasted the pine nuts in the oven, kalamati olives, lemon and Girard's Greek salad dressing. Cooked the Orzo in chicken broth as recommended and it was fine. Not too salty. Added the pepper flakes. Waited to add Feta until salad was completely cooled. Really excellent!

I have made this recipe at least a dozen times. I always make it with fresh herbs and plain feta. I have made it with just the ingredients listed, but sometimes I add things like artichoke hearts, sun dried tomatoes, or lemon zest. It tastes best If you make in the day before, although the fresh basil does get dark. I usually halve it for just my husband and myself. Fantastic recipe!

Absolutely LOVED THIS! I did not cook my orzo in chicken broth nor did I add the butter to it after, just rinsed. I only had regular (light) feta so used that & decided not to use the juice from the capers but did add more fresh lemon juice to compensate. Made this to go along with Feta Cheese Turkey Burgers/Spicy Turkey Burgers from this site for our youngest son's 2nd birthday with our families. SO GOOD...will certainly make this one again, hubby proclaimed as his new fave orzo salad!

Absolutely amazing. My husband said that this is his favorite meal that I've ever made...and I cook quite a bit. My meal had a few changes...substituted quinoa for the orzo. Instead of spinach, I used romaine lettuce and also added cubed turkey at the end. Made enough for leftovers and can't wait to eat some today!

Oh, wow. This is SO GOOD! Excellent combination of flavors and textures. The only changes I made were to use veg broth and fresh herbs (I added the basil with the spinach rather than sauteing it), and olive oil instead of butter. I'll dry-toast the nuts next time--they seemed a little soggy from toasting in the oil, and my garlic started to burn. Still, absolutely delicious--a new favorite!

This was really good! I left out the capers because I don’t like them, but I made everything else according to the recipe. I actually halved the ingredients because 8 servings seemed like a lot, and I’m glad I did because it filled a 3-1/2 qt. casserole dish! I recommend that if you half the recipe like I did, to half everything except the garlic, thyme, basil, and crushed pepper; those you should you use the full amounts listed. I also added a little extra lemon juice to make up for omitting the capers. Overall it was very good, and can easily be tweaked to fit your tastes.
I did cut this in half, it makes allot! I love lemon so I added a fair amount more. Otherwise, GREAT recipe.
Yummy! Didn’t have pine nuts, used almonds and diced them up. Definitely a recipe I will be using often this summer!

Yum! I really enjoyed this orzo salad, especially as leftovers the next couple of days after making it! It was a nice, light break from the heavier pasta salads we can get so used to. I didn't change a thing. I think there is a lot of room for variation and experimentation everytime you make this - for example, roasted red peppers would probably be awesome in this dish. Make it your own!
So good! I didn’t have pine nuts so I used crushed mixed nuts and I added a can of tuna. It was perfect.
My family enjoyed this salad. It makes A LOT, so use a big bowl. Because of the volume I did not use all of the spinach the recipe called for, but it still turned out really good.
Added grilled chicken for protein. Delicious!!!
Excellent recipe. A little too salty as written. I used only one tablespoon of capers which worked well.

My mom makes this several times over the summer. My father and son love it. My Mom is asked to make it for potlucks. She puts in diced tomatoes(1 contioner of grape tomatoes), and goat cheese instead of feta cheese.

Really good. Followed the recipe as-is except I just used a bit of olive oil to stop the cooked orzo from sticking. I also used less pine nuts and just put them on at the end, on top, as garnish. Smelled heavenly, tasted very good chilled. We're in a heat wave now where I live, so this was refreshing to have cold for supper.
